 Order

This Criminal Petition is filed by the petitioners seeking to quash the proceedings in Crime No.48/2022 for the offences under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. Brief facts of the case are as under:
It is the case of the prosecution that the complainant married Rahul Gada on 29.04.2016.
At the time of the marriage, it is stated that dowry was given in the form of cash, gold, silver and also household articles.
It is stated in the complaint that she was taken care only for 15 days.
Thereafter, the petitioners used to demand to bring additional dowry and also abusing her in filthy language.
It is further stated that the complainant was being harassed both mentally and physically in connection with demand of dowry.
It is stated that in the meantime, the complainant had been to Bengaluru to stay with her husband.
It is stated in the complaint that even all the petitioners had also been to Bengaluru stayed for some days with the complainant and accused No.1.
In the meantime, the complainant became pregnant and delivered a female child.

It is stated that the petitioners were insulting the complainant as she Venkata Ramani And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43661352/
2 gave birth to a female child.

sentences.text: The complainant had been subjected to cruelty every day in one or the other pretext.

Such being the fact, on 10.02.2020 at about 8-00 a.m.,
when the complainant was at her house in Bengaluru, the accused No.1/husband of the complainant started quarreling with her demanding the car as a dowry and assaulted her.
When the complainant refused to yield his demand, she was thrown out of the house along with the child.
Consequently, it is constrained her to stay with her parents' house at Bidar.
It is stated in the complaint that the alleged demand of dowry and harassment made by the petitioners since 13.05.2016 up to 10.02.2020.
Hence, a complaint came to be lodged on 31.07.2022.
The police have registered the case in Crime No.48/2022 for the above said offences.

3. Heard Sri Aditya Sondhi, learned senior counsel appearing on behalf of Sri Basavaraj M. Police Patil, Sri Ajay Jawali and Sri Mallikarjun B.M., learned counsel for the petitioners, Sri Gururaj V.
Hasilkar, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Sri Kadloor Satyanarayanacharya, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
4.

It is the submission of the learned counsel of the petitioners that respondent No.2 made out omnibus allegations against the petitioners, who are the mother-in-law, the father-in- law, the brother-in-law and the sister-in-law.

Even taking into consideration the averments of the complaint,
the respondent No.2 was living at Bengaluru along with accused No.1 separately from the house of her in-laws.
It is further submitted that respondent No.2 made allegations that she was being harassed humiliated, degraded at the hands of her in-laws in connection with demand of dowry.
However, even on reading the complaint in its entirety, the possibilities of getting them convicted is very bleak and negligible.

Therefore, asking the petitioners to face the trial on such trivial grounds,
obviously, is an abuse of process of law.
Hence, the petition deserves to be allowed.

5. The learned senior counsel further brought to the notice of this Court that petitioner Nos.3 and 4 are residing at Hyderabad and they have been falsely implicated and roped in this case to harass them.
Making such submissions, the learned senior counsel for the petitioners prays to allow the petition and quash the proceedings.

6. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1/State vehemently opposed the petition stating that respondent No.2 specifically made out a case against the petitioners and overt-act of each petitioner has been explained properly.
The averments of the complaint clearly disclose about the triable issues.
Such being the fact, it would not be appropriate to scuttle down the proceedings before conducting the trial.
Making such submissions, the learned High Court Government Pleader prays to dismiss the petition.

7. The learned counsel for respondent No.2 vehemently opposed the petition submitting that the petitioner Nos.1 and 2 being the mother-in-law and father-in-law used to demand additional dowry and also harassed the respondent No.2 for having given birth to a female child and petitioner Nos.3 and 4 were also demanding the dowry and instigating the accused No.1 to give torture and harassment to the complainant.
The averments need to be tried in a full-fledged trial.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: After having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments made in the complaint, now it is necessary to delve upon the nature and content of allegations made in the complaint.

The entire allegations appears to be omnibus in nature and there are no specific overt-acts attributed against the petitioners and it appears that the respondent No.2 after the marriage, she was residing at Bengaluru along with accused No.1 and she gave birth to a female child and after completion of post natal period, again she joined the company of her husband and there is a specific allegation made out against accused No.1 that, on 10.02.2020 the accused No.1 had demanded dowry, as the complainant did not hear him, she was thrown out from the matrimonial house.

9. Now, it is relevant to refer the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of K. Subba Rao vs. The State of Telangana1, wherein it is observed that:
"6. The Court should be careful in proceeding against distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: K. Subba Rao vs. The State of Telangana1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out."
10.
Coming to the facts of the case, admittedly the marriage of respondent No.2 was solemnized on 29.04.2016 and (2018) 14 SCC 452 she was residing with accused No.1 at Bengaluru till 10.02.2020.
Nowhere it is stated that she stayed along with the petitioners.
It appears from the records that petitioner Nos.3 and 4 are the residents of Hyderabad.
Prima facie, the allegations made against all the petitioners are omnibus, absurd and vexatious.
Even on reading the complaint in its entirety, the allegations made out against the petitioners are not sufficient to face the trial.
11. It is needless to say that respondent No.2 allegedly thrown out by her husband from matrimonial home on 10.02.2020 and a complaint came to be lodged on 31.07.2022.

There is inordinate delay,
the delay has not been explained by respondent No.2.
Obviously, the delay would defeat the case of the prosecution.

It is necessary to consider the delay in lodging the complaint in matrimonial cases,
at par with other complaints in general.
The delay in lodging the complaint certainly would affect the credibility of the complaint and the alleged incident in other IPC offences.
Similarly, even if the delay is caused in lodging the complaint in matrimonial issues, certainly would also affect the case of the prosecution.

Therefore, the petition deserves to be allowed not only on the ground of bald,
vexatious and omnibus allegations but also on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.

Hence,
it is a fit case to exercise the inherent jurisdiction to quash the proceedings.

12. In the light of the observations made above, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The FIR in Crime No.48/2022, registered by the Women Police Station, Bidar,
pending on the file of the I Additional JMFC Court, Bidar is quashed.
